culturalBackground: Rajasthani, or Marwari, mehndi is known for dense, very fine detail that covers the whole hand.
Sojat, in Rajasthan's Pali district, is India's best-known henna-growing area.
Designs often include figures such as a bride and groom, peacocks and elephants.
Mirrored designs, where the two hands form one picture when held together, are a hallmark of the style.
applicationTips: Use a very fine cone tip; Rajasthani detail is too small for a standard tip.
Divide the hand into panels first and fill one at a time.
Allow plenty of time, since dense coverage takes much longer than open styles.

faqPool.q: What is special about Rajasthani mehndi?
faqPool.a: Its very fine, dense detail and its use of figures such as the bride, groom, peacocks and elephants.

faqPool.q: What is a mirrored mehndi design?
faqPool.a: It is a design drawn so that the two hands match or join into one image when placed side by side.
It is worn at weddings and at festivals such as Teej and Gangaur, which are widely celebrated in Rajasthan.
